quotes.text: The best way to predict the future is to invent it.
quotes.author: Alan Kay

quotes.text: Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.
quotes.author: Arthur C. Clarke

quotes.text: If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.
quotes.author: Isaac Newton

quotes.text: Anyone who has never made a mistake has never tried anything new.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein

quotes.text: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
quotes.author: Will Durant

quotes.text: The function of good software is to make the complex appear simple.
quotes.author: Grady Booch

quotes.text: An investment in knowledge pays the best interest.
quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin

quotes.text: Talk is cheap. Show me the code.
quotes.author: Linus Torvalds

quotes.text: Programs must be written for people to read, and only incidentally for machines to execute.
quotes.author: Harold Abelson

quotes.text: What we know is a drop. What we don't know is an ocean.
quotes.author: Isaac Newton

quotes.text: Logic will get you from A to Z. Imagination will get you everywhere.
quotes.author: Albert Einstein

quotes.text: If you cannot measure it, you cannot improve it.
quotes.author: Lord Kelvin

quotes.text: Make it work, make it right, make it fast.
quotes.author: Kent Beck

quotes.text: Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.
quotes.author: Thomas Edison

quotes.text: The cure for boredom is curiosity. There is no cure for curiosity.
quotes.author: Dorothy Parker

quotes.text: It always seems impossible until it is done.
quotes.author: Nelson Mandela

facts: Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood. Two pump blood to the gills, the third pumps it everywhere else.
Honey never spoils. Archaeologists have found 3,000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs that's still edible.
A day on Venus is longer than a year. Venus rotates so slowly that one rotation (243 Earth days) outlasts its orbit (225 days).
Bananas are berries, but strawberries are not. Botanically, a true berry develops from a single ovary.
The Eiffel Tower can grow up to 15 cm taller in summer due to thermal expansion of its iron.
Wombats produce cube-shaped poop. They're the only animal in the world that does this.
There are more possible chess games than there are atoms in the observable universe.
Sharks are older than trees. Sharks have existed for ~400 million years; the earliest trees only ~350 million.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
The shortest war in history lasted 38 minutes — fought between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896.
A single cumulus cloud can weigh more than a million pounds, despite floating effortlessly above us.
Octopuses can taste with their suckers — each one has thousands of chemical receptors.
The Pacific Ocean is wider than the Moon.
Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
Bees can recognize human faces. They use the same techniques humans do — assembling features into a whole.
There is enough DNA in your body, uncoiled, to stretch from Earth to Pluto and back — 17 times.
The unicorn is Scotland's national animal.
Hot water can freeze faster than cold water under certain conditions — known as the Mpemba effect.
The oldest known living tree is a bristlecone pine in California, estimated at over 4,800 years old.
A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh about 6 billion tons on Earth.

words.def: The pleasant earthy scent produced when rain falls on dry soil.
words.example: The first rain of summer brought a wave of petrichor through the open windows.

words.def: The realization that each random passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as your own.
words.example: Walking through the crowded station, she was struck by a sudden wave of sonder.

words.def: The act of throwing someone or something out of a window.
words.example: The Defenestration of Prague in 1618 helped trigger the Thirty Years' War.

words.def: Sweet, smooth, or musical; pleasing to hear.
words.example: Her mellifluous voice carried easily across the auditorium.

words.def: A deep emotional state of nostalgic longing for an absent something or someone.
words.example: Old fado songs filled him with saudade for a Lisbon he had never seen.

words.def: A state of human flourishing; the highest good in Aristotelian ethics.
words.example: Aristotle argued that eudaimonia comes from a life of virtue and reason.

words.def: Endless and futile, like the labor of Sisyphus, condemned to roll a boulder uphill forever.
words.example: Cleaning a toddler's room can feel like a Sisyphean task.

words.def: Exceedingly idealistic; unrealistic and impractical, after Don Quixote.
words.example: His quixotic plan to bicycle across the Sahara surprised everyone.

words.def: A homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or that never was.
words.example: A decade abroad left her with a deep hiraeth she couldn't quite name.

words.def: The warmth of the sun in winter.
words.example: The cat curled on the windowsill, basking in the apricity of January.

words.def: Having a strong religious or spiritual quality; mysterious and awe-inspiring.
words.example: Standing at the edge of the canyon at dawn felt almost numinous.

words.def: Too great or extreme to be expressed in words.
words.example: The view from the summit was ineffable — no photo could do it justice.
